netlifyRouting: Declares `export const config = { path: '/api/userinfo' }` (userinfo.ts:32): served on that path directly as a Functions v2 custom path, independent of the netlify.toml /api/* rewrite.

methodHandling.otherMethods: Not checked; every method is handled identically.

auth.notes: Does NOT use requireUser and does NOT verify the token signature, issuer, audience or expiry. It base64-decodes the JWT payload segment. The DEV_SECRET_KEY bypass is not supported (a dev key with no '.' gives 401 Invalid token). It is an OIDC userinfo shim for Supabase Auth's custom:auxi provider (DETAILED-PLAN.md C8).

request.parse: token = Authorization header with a leading /^Bearer\s+/i removed (userinfo.ts:3). Any header value without that prefix is used whole as the token.

fields.name: Authorization header
fields.validation: empty after stripping -> 401 Unauthorized; JWT payload = token.split('.')[1], '-'->'+', '_'->'/', atob, JSON.parse

checkOrder: 2. decode payload (:10-12), any throw -> 401 Invalid token (:27-29)

responses.when: payload decodes and has an email

errors.contentType: text/plain;charset=UTF-8 (no content-type header is set, so the Response default for a string body applies)
errors.when: no Authorization header, or 'Bearer ' with nothing after it
payload decodes but has none of emails[0], email, upn

body.detail: String(e), e.g. "TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'replace')" (no '.' in token), "InvalidCharacterError: The string to be decoded is not correctly encoded." (bad base64 length), "InvalidCharacterError: Invalid character", or a JSON SyntaxError message

errors.when: payload segment missing, not base64, or not JSON

quirks: Error responses carry no content-type header; only the 200 sets application/json. Bodies are still JSON text.

The 401 'Invalid token' body has an extra `detail` member with the JS exception text, which depends on the runtime (strings above observed on Node v24.15.0). This is the only route with {error, detail}.
No signature verification: any well-formed JWT-shaped string with an email claim yields 200.

atob() returns a Latin-1 binary string, so non-ASCII UTF-8 claims come out garbled: a name 'José' is returned as 'JosÃ©' (verified with Node v24.15.0). A Python port that decodes UTF-8 properly would change the output.
A token in a non-Bearer header ('Basic x.y.z') is still decoded, because only a Bearer prefix is stripped.
Claims with undefined values are omitted from the JSON (JSON.stringify drops undefined).

callers.where: configured in Supabase (not in this repo); sign-in entry at src/pages/SignIn.tsx:15,24 per DETAILED-PLAN.md C8

docs.openapi: public/openapi.yaml:1709-1740. Discrepancies: claims 'With the dev bypass key, returns the dev@sales.invalid identity' - false, the handler never checks DEV_SECRET_KEY, a dev key without '.' returns 401 {error:'Invalid token', detail}; 400 and 401 responses undocumented; says it decodes 'identity claims' without noting B2C `emails`/`oid`/`upn` precedence.
docs.postman: docs/postman_collection.json '7.1 Inspect JWT (userinfo)': uses the collection's dev_key bearer, which yields 401 Invalid token, not identity claims.

planSection65: Row says `IdP bearer -> {email, name, given_name, family_name}; 400 {error:"No email in token"}, 401`. Correction: the 200 body also includes `sub` (oid || sub); the 401 has two bodies ({error:'Unauthorized'} and {error:'Invalid token', detail}); error responses have no content-type header.
